recommendations.threadTitle: Ask HN: Best books on AI?
recommendations.threadContext: The asker wanted practical AI books without much prior knowledge. Replies debate the need for theory and mathematical foundations.
recommendations.author: arihant
recommendations.quote: You cannot really go practical in AI without academic rigor.
recommendations.context: Recommends this first, followed by Deep Learning. The recommendation explicitly includes academic study.

recommendations.author: brogrammer2
recommendations.quote: Though it is an academic book, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach by Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig. The first chapter in the book provides a detailed analysis of how other disciplines contribute to the idea of AI - from Philosophy to Psychology, Biology to Computer Science. Makes for an interesting read, even for a non-tech reader.
recommendations.context: Recommends AIMA while explicitly acknowledging its academic character and praising the interdisciplinary opening chapter.

recommendations.author: metaobject
recommendations.quote: PAIP is also very, very high on my list as well. I'm very pro-lisp and still develop new projects in lisp (CL, Scheme) and promote it when/where I can. But the person who picks up PAIP wanting to learn AI might not necessarily want to worry about picking up lisp programming skills at the same time (nor is learning lisp strictly necessary). This is why AIMA is still the best option, IMO, because it employs a language agnostic approach.
